P1: `evidence/m326_mutate.txt:4-27`, `scripts/m326_mutate.py:34-39`

The mutation harness is a declared-set checker, not an independent verifier of gate coverage.
It records each mutant’s actual reddened set (`red=...`), compares it with an authored
`declared` set, and only fails if they differ; it never checks that the declared set is
sufficient to make the claimed gate fail.

That is visible in `evidence/m326_mutate_measure.txt`, which proves the harness’s own
declared sets were initially wrong:

- `evidence/m326_mutate_measure.txt:18`
  `MU13 ... red=G1,G2,G6,G9 ... declared=G1,G2 ... MISMATCH`
- `evidence/m326_mutate_measure.txt:25`
  `MU23 ... red=G3 ... declared=G1,G2,G3 ... MISMATCH`

So at least two “OK” rows in the shipped evidence (`evidence/m326_mutate.txt:17`, `:22`) are
not real independent checks; they are assertions that the authors’ declared set happened to
match a measured sweep that already revealed two misdeclared mutants.

Why it matters: under the repo law, every `VERIFIED` row must be reddened by a mutant that
actually makes the claimed gate fail. Here the harness only enforces
`measured == authored`. If the authored set is too small or too large, the harness can be
“green” while some `VERIFIED` claim is either:

- not actually reddened by the claimed mutant, or
- only accidentally reddened by an unrelated collateral gate.

This is not cosmetic. It lets the PR certify rows against the wrong mutants. For example,
row 1 of `NAMED.md` (`NAMED.md:1297`) cites `MU4/9/12-17/19/20/23` for claims backed by
`G1-G3`, but the evidence shows `MU4` reddens only `G5` (`evidence/m326_mutate.txt:8`), not
`G1-G3`. The harness passes because `declared={G5}` equals measured `red={G5}`; it does not
catch that the claim-to-mutant mapping in `NAMED.md` is wrong.

This undermines the central anti-decoration mechanism for the PR.

---

P1: `NAMED.md:1302` (`M325 QUALIFIED` row), `evidence/m326_block224_census.txt:32` (`T10`)

The claim
> `29 prov labels BLKCONST->STRIDE +4 UNPROVEN det under fix; all pins/totals unchanged`

is marked `V MU17`, but `T10` is not a shipped gate assertion. It is only a printed
diagnostic (`scripts/m326_block224_census.py:946`). The script has no gate object for
`T10`; the census summary is still `9/9` (`scripts/m326_block224_census.py:1038`), and the
mutation harness only parses `G1..G9` (`scripts/m326_mutate.py:31-33`, `:51-55`).

So `MU17` reddens `G2` (`evidence/m326_mutate.txt:21`), i.e. the M326 prov pins, but there is
no gate that asserts the M325 cross-check counts or the “all pins/totals unchanged” claim. If
a future code path or parser change altered `T10` without breaking `G1-G9`, this `VERIFIED`
row would remain marked green.

Why it matters: this is exactly the class of defect the conventions target—“digest/printed
measurement only,” not an acceptance gate. `T10` is hashed into the census digest, but the
harness does not require the digest to match any fixed value; it only requires `9/9` and
declared mutant sets. So the claim can become false without reddening a gate.

---

P1: `NAMED.md:1303` (`ACCEPT` row)

The row is marked `V`, but its evidence field is literally just:

```md
| ACCEPT ... | cite | V |
```

No `path:line`. The conventions require every `VERIFIED` claim to cite concrete evidence.
This row is the highest-level certification row in the milestone, and it currently has no
machine-checkable evidence pointer in the table itself.

Why it matters: the table is the artifact that maps claims to gates/evidence. A bare
`cite` defeats auditability and lets the most important claim float without a shipped
assertion reference.

---

P1: `NAMED.md:1298`, `scripts/m326_block224_census.py:875-880`, `evidence/m326_block224_census.txt:34`

The claim
> `13 hits 3W/10R all dw (0 ABS/DISP224/sub); W={41a543 add,520b22 zero,59f0c1 reset}; 0 seeds; 13/13 STRIDE under subreg-fix (ALGO7=old blindness)`

is partly a definition mismatch with the gate.

`G1` pins:

- hit count = 13
- writers = 3
- readers = 10
- `n_abs == 0`
- `n_224 == 0`
- `n_sub == 0`
- writer sites == `[0x41a543, 0x520b22, 0x59f0c1]`
- reader sites == hardcoded 10 addresses

(`scripts/m326_block224_census.py:845-853`)

But `G1` never checks:

- that those three writer sites are respectively an `add`, a zero-store, and the reset-store;
- that the hits are “all dw” except by a global width equality against `len(rows)` (`:842`).

That second one is acceptable-ish because every row is width-checked against the row count,
but the first one is not. The prose names semantic writer roles (`add`, `zero`, `reset`)
inside a row attributed to `G1-G3`, yet the role distinction is established by `G4/G5/G7`
later, not by `G1`.

Why it matters: the row says one thing, the cited gate reads a weaker/orthogonal thing. If
the writer set stayed identical but instruction semantics changed in a way `G4/G5/G7` did
not catch, the claim “3W={add, zero, reset}” would drift from `G1`. This is the sort of
claim-to-gate scope mismatch the reviewer law is supposed to prevent.

---

P2: `NAMED.md:1301`, `scripts/m326_block224_census.py:892-906`, `evidence/m326_block224_census.txt:39`

The claim
> `all 10 readers = 220-224 AVAILABLE (itoa 64f980); cheat-cap MIN(g999fa4,avail)@41a4e0-f9`

is stronger than `G6` actually measures.

`G6` checks (`scripts/m326_block224_census.py:892-906`):

1. a hardcoded list of 10 triples exists;
2. each triple contains substrings `0x94d650` and `0x94d654`;
3. `len(triples) == len(readers)`;
4. one global `itoa` call shape at `0x416987/0x4169b5`;
5. one global cheat-cap shape at `0x41a4e0..0x41a4fe`.

That does not establish “all 10 readers = AVAILABLE” semantically.

Problems:

- The triple check is substring-based, not structural. It never proves the two loads feed the
  same base register, nor that the subtraction’s destination is the value ultimately used.
  A reader could read a 220 from one block context and a 224 from another and still satisfy
  the substring test.
- The `itoa` pin is only measured for one site. The prose ties `AVAILABLE` to `itoa` as if
  the reader set jointly establishes it, but `G6` only verifies one `push 0xa / call 0x64f980`
  instance (`:884-885`).
- The cheat-cap pin is only measured for one site. The wording makes it sound like a shared
  property of the reader law, but it is one local consumer check.

Why it matters: this is a source-only / partial-site measurement being sold as a whole-set
semantic claim. It passes for the current binary but does not actually read the claim in the
scope asserted by the prose.

---

P2: `NAMED.md:1299`, `scripts/m326_block224_census.py:854-868`, `evidence/m326_block224_census.txt:34`

The row says:

> `13/13 STRIDE under subreg-fix (ALGO7=old blindness)`

`G2` does pin all 13 provenances, so the fact is measured. But the “subreg-fix” framing is
not actually gated end-to-end by the shipped mutation evidence for this row.

The mechanism mutant is `MU17` (`M326_ALGO=7`), and `MU17` reddens `G2`
(`evidence/m326_mutate.txt:21`). That shows old blindness breaks the current pins.

However, the fix itself is asserted by source text matching in `m325_crosscheck()`:

- `scripts/m326_block224_census.py:971-980`
  It replaces M325 source with a fixed snippet and injects `PARTIALS` by string replace.
- If M325 source moves or its anchors change, this function can degrade into `{error: ...}`
  (`:977-979`), yet no gate asserts the absence of that error.
- The printed `T10` line includes that dict verbatim, and the digest hashes it (`:1016`),
  but again there is no `T10` gate.

Why it matters: the PR’s central self-found instrument correction is validated by a printed
crosscheck, not by an assertion that the correction applied cleanly. A future refactor of
M325 could make the crosscheck emit an error string, preserve all `G1-G9`, and leave the
“under subreg-fix” claim effectively unenforced.

---

P2: `scripts/m326_block224_census.py:982-1001`, `evidence/m326_block224_census.txt:32`

`m325_crosscheck()` reports “unchanged pins/totals” by constructing aggregate counts
(`hits`, `regwr`, `regrd`, `seeds`) and a diff list, but it does not re-assert the
M325 gate pins themselves.

For example, it checks:

- census hit set equality (`:983-986`)
- `prov` label equality per address (`:987-991`)
- reg-write / reg-read tuple equality (`:992-999`)
- seed count equality (`:996-997`)

That is strong evidence, but the claim in `NAMED.md:1302` says “all pins/totals unchanged.”
The code does not verify M325’s own shipped gate pins (`M325 G3`, `M325 G4`, etc.); it
verifies only a subset of related counts. In particular, if some M325 gate pinned something
not re-derived here, `M325 QUALIFIED` could overstate the safety of the fix.

Why it matters: the row is not just “the diff list looks unchanged”; it is “M325 gates
stand.” The instrument does not mechanically re-read M325’s gate expectations, so the claim
is stronger than the measurement.

---

P2: `scripts/m326_block224_census.py:620-627`, `scripts/m326_block224_census.py:700-704`

The resolver’s partial-register fix is incomplete: it treats only partial destinations as
opaque definitions of a wider queried register (`dest in PARTIALS.get(reg, ())`).

But the inverse case is missing:

- when `value_of(..., "al")` is asked, a full-register write to `eax` is **not** treated as a
  definition of `al`;
- same for `ax`, `si/di/bp/sp`, etc.

This is visible directly in the code path:

```python
if dest != reg:
    if ALGO != "7" and dest in PARTIALS.get(reg, ()):
        return ("lin", 1, 0, ("arg", reg))
    continue
```

So for `reg="al"`, `dest="eax"` does **not** match `PARTIALS["al"]` and is skipped.

Why it matters: this is the exact class of over-proof the PR claims to fix. Right now the
measured claims may survive because they mostly query full registers, but the instrument’s
own stated law (“partial-register writes are opaque”) is not implemented completely. That
makes future claims about leaf provenance fragile and potentially false.

---

P2: `scripts/m326_block224_census.py:679-749`, `scripts/m326_block224_census.py:752-797`

`seed_scan()` breaks on full-register redefinition of the seed register, but not on
partial-register redefinition of that same seed register:

```python
d2 = reg_of(parts2[0])
if d2 == dest and mn2 not in ("cmp", "test"):
    break
```

Again, this misses the inverse subreg case:

- seed register = `eax`
- intervening instruction = `mov al, ...`

The scanner will continue treating `[eax+d]` as still tracking the original address, even
though the low byte changed and the full address is no longer known.

Why it matters: `G3` pins the seed-access totals and “sibling-offset-into-224=0”
(`scripts/m326_block224_census.py:871-876`, `evidence/m326_block224_census.txt:36`). The
seed scanner is the instrument that justifies that claim, but it can keep a stale seed past
a partial invalidation. That is a real correctness gap in the measurement, not just a
theoretical robustness issue.

---

P2: `evidence/m326_block224_census.txt:42`, `scripts/m326_block224_census.py:921-931`

The save claim is stronger than the pinned gate wording.

Claim:

> `save [0]*8 @550+k*20bc raw block carry ...`

`G8` pins:

- `sv["off"] == 0x32c`
- per-block `vals == [0]*8`
- energy array
- file hash / size / year / round / gap / gapval
- codec leg instructions
- `0x105e0 == NBLK * STRIDE`

But it does **not** directly pin the printed file offsets list `T8b` as a gate condition, nor
does the digest include that exact derived list separately. The digest includes `(sv, leg)`
(`:1011`), but not `field-file-offsets` itself (`scripts/m326_block224_census.py:799-801`).

Why it matters: the prose gives a concrete byte-layout formula (`@550+k*20bc`). The gate
reads a nearby invariant (`off == 0x32c`) and the field values, but the exact printed
formula is not independently pinned in the acceptance surface. This is a narrow scope
mismatch, but it is the kind of “measurement exists in output, not asserted as claim” issue
the law targets.
